Ekinci Named Chief Operating Officer at Turkauto as Firm Eyes Growth in Turkish Automotive Market

Turkauto, a leading player in Turkey’s automotive sector, has appointed Selin Ekinci as its new Chief Operating Officer, effective immediately. Ekinci, an industry veteran with over two decades of experience in manufacturing and supply chain management, steps into the role as the company looks to expand its operations within the fast-evolving Turkish automotive landscape.

Ekinci previously served as Executive Vice President for Production at OtomotivTek, where she was credited with implementing advanced lean manufacturing principles and driving operational efficiencies across multiple facilities. At Turkauto, she will report directly to CEO Kadir Yılmaz and oversee all domestic production, logistics and supplier relations.

“Selin brings a wealth of operational expertise and a proven track record of leadership in automotive manufacturing,” said Yılmaz in a statement. “Her appointment is a key part of our strategy to strengthen Turkauto’s position as a leading manufacturer and to capitalize on new opportunities in Turkey and the broader region.”

The Turkish automotive industry, one of the country’s largest export sectors, has seen strong domestic sales and a rebound in exports, with the Automotive Manufacturers Association reporting a 12% year-on-year increase in vehicle output in the first quarter of 2024. As the sector increasingly embraces electrification and digitalization, experienced operational leadership is seen as critical.

Industry analysts welcomed the appointment. “Ekinci’s operational background and her experience with digital transformation projects will be invaluable as Turkauto navigates ongoing shifts in consumer demand and regulatory requirements,” said Ali Demir, senior analyst at Mobility Insights Istanbul.

The Turkish Automotive Workers’ Union also expressed support. “We look forward to working with Ms. Ekinci to ensure workforce stability and skills development amid ongoing technological change,” said union president Nihat Karaca.

In her first comments as COO, Ekinci emphasized her commitment to innovation and collaboration. “I am excited to join Turkauto at a time of significant opportunity for the Turkish automotive industry,” she said. “My focus will be on operational excellence, sustainability and empowering our teams for future challenges.”

Turkauto did not disclose any immediate changes to its corporate strategy, but stated that Ekinci will lead an internal review of production processes in coming months.
